title: Myanmar has been found guilty of genocide. Should Israel be worried? – podcast
summary: The international court of justice has for the first time ruled that a state has committed genocide. Yasmin Ullah explains what it means for the Rohingya people, while Kaamil Ahmed lays out how the case unfolded For seven years, Yasmin Ullah had been part of the delegation arguing that Myanmar had committed genocide – one of the gravest human rights crimes – against Rohingya Muslims. The genocide has directly affected Yasmin and her family. Last week she was in court to hear the international court of justice’s landmark verdict against Myanmar. “I was really kind of pinching myself. It felt like we were all able to breathe again,” she tells Annie Kelly. Continue reading...
authors: Presented by Annie Kelly with Kaamil Ahmed, produced by George McDonagh, Harriet Mogie and Rudi Zygadlo

title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
summary: Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1 Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’ Play through 22 famous world championship games The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez ( 1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6 ), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess. The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4. Continue reading...

title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
summary: Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain. A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination. Continue reading...
authors: Cris Seda Chabrier in New York

title: After 80 years in Oxford, Naga ancestors are finally going home
summary: A campaign securing the landmark return to India of ancestral remains taken during British colonial rule has opened a wider conversation about restitution • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The lacerating legacy of colonialism survives in many spaces, particularly in museum collections and private holdings across the western world. And it’s not just limited to inanimate artefacts or cultural objects. For almost 80 years, human remains were displayed on crowded glass shelves at Pitt Rivers Museum at Oxford University, one of the world’s most celebrated institutions. Continue reading...

title: Canada says it ‘does not report to the US’ after Pentagon criticizes military spending
summary: Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour. The document , released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”. Continue reading...

title: Israel attempts to jail Palestinian student at Hebrew University without trial
summary: Mahdi Tounsi appeared to have suffered maltreatment at hearing where he was not allowed to hear prosecution case against him Palestinian student Mahdi Tounsi appeared in a closed-door court hearing in Jerusalem, as academics and activists warned that Israel’s attempt to jail him without trial marked a serious escalation in attacks on Palestinian rights. Yael Berda, a lawyer and sociology professor at Hebrew University, who has taught Tounsi for four years, came to court to call for his release. Continue reading...
authors: Emma Graham-Harrison and Quique Kierszenbaum in Jerusalem

title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
summary: Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests. Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May . Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged. Continue reading...

title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
summary: Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted. “Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.” Continue reading...
authors: Pjotr Sauer, Michael Goodier, Harriet Agerholm, Philip McMahon and Carmen Aguilar García
